items.title: Bill Charlap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: Jimmy Rowles said something great that I remember. In an interview he said something about if you have an idea play half of it.

ctx.x: When you’re playing in a situation like you did this afternoon with Roland Hanna, there was some pretty adventurous things that happened between you two. Had you guys done that before?

We’ve played two pianos once, one song. And it was like that immediately. And that was many years ago, so, not that many, maybe two or three. You listen. We have a frame of reference. We can talk about things musically. He can play a chord and I know what chord he’s playing. Or he can get into a rhythmic idea or a feel or a groove, and I know what he’s talking about. Or, we might go on a flight of fancy where it’s like well we might make it, we might not. You know it’s a trapeze act. You see a great family, they…
Right. Leave half left over for some other time too.
